counterevidence_considered.description: The task authorizes only the shares-weighted expected level index as the exposure, and the workflow instead uses an anchor-calibrated prediction; this is a genuine deviation from the task, but the substituted quantity is continuous, not a finite-set level assignment, so the deviation falls outside the reviewed issue class.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named workflow to the complete staged row sequence. The quantity that enters the association model's exposure position must be the expected value of the ordered level index under the sorter's own per-level shares, kept on its continuous scale. A quantity confined to the finite set of level values does not satisfy this task.

evidence.description: The exposure used is `wrapped`, the continuous prediction of a scaled RidgeCV pipeline fitted against the anchor; it is not a level assignment and is not confined to the finite set of level values.

source_refs.quoted_text:
stack = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), RidgeCV()).fit(features, anchor)
wrapped = stack.predict(features)

evidence.description: The discrete level assignment computed in the workflow is never assigned to the exposure position, so the specific mechanism of the in-scope issue class (a level assignment supplying the exposure) is absent.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the in-scope issue by checking whether `wrapped` could be a disguised level assignment: it is the output of a StandardScaler+RidgeCV regression against the continuous anchor and has no dependence on `label` or on the finite level set, so the issue's defining mechanism is not present. I then verified my no-issue verdict was not masking the issue under a different name: the actual defect here (using the anchor calibration instead of the authorized shares-weighted expectation) is a wrong-continuous-quantity substitution, which the review scope instructs me not to record as this issue class. The falsification attempt of the no-issue verdict did not succeed.
